transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-11-20
Time: 16:00 PST
Duration: 45m
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE); Laura Chen (Redwood SE); Maya Rios (NovaHealth, Head of ML Ops); Daniel Cho (NovaHealth, Platform Engineer); Priya Mehta (NovaHealth, CTO)

Summary (auto): Quick Console walkthrough focusing on usage analytics, per-route dashboards, and cost breakdown. Discussed Optimize recommendations (batching, caching, model profiles) and security questions (VPC, KMS, SOC2). Agreed to run pilot benchmark and share pricing/security docs.

Topics: Console analytics overview; per-route dashboards; cost attribution and breakdown; Optimize recommendations; Dedicated vs Hosted tradeoffs; next steps & pilot plan.

Transcript:
[00:00] Samir: hey everyone, thanks for joining — we'll do a quick console walkthrough, call out the usage analytics, per-route dashboards and how cost breaks down, and then leave time for q's.
[00:16] Maya: awesome, thanks. quick context — we've got latency-sensitive clinical-assist features, and cost is a big blocker, so want to see how you surface per-route costs.
[00:29] Laura: great, that's exactly what we'll show. i'm going to share my screen — bear with the permission popups.
[00:45] Laura: ok, so this is the Redwood Console, landing page, you can see top-line usage: total tokens, requests, avg latency. right away you can filter by model, by route, by time window.
[01:05] Daniel: looks clean. where does the token calc come from? do you normalize across different model tokenizers?
[01:15] Laura: good question — we use model-specific tokenization profiles; in the UI we normalize to token units so you can compare costs. small caveat: sometimes the tokenizer names show up slightly different in the transcript export — like GPT-4 style names may appear as G-P-T 4.
[01:30] Priya: are these raw infra costs or include redwood margin?
[01:36] Samir: by default the usage pane shows Redwood billable units and a cost estimate based on model profile & infra selection; for committed Dedicated customers we can plug in your committed unit price so the per-route USD changes.
[01:50] Laura: switching to per-route dashboards. here you see a list of routes — each route has tokens, request counts, p90 latency, errors, and a cost column. you can click into any route to see time series and token distribution (prompt vs completion).
[02:12] Laura: i'll open the /clinical-note-gen route. notice the breakdown: 68% of tokens are completions, 32% prompts; avg p95 latency ~320ms on hosted.
[02:28] Maya: that matches our expectation; completions are large. can you show where caching helps?
[02:34] Laura: yeah — under Optimize suggestions (we also push these as alerts) you'll see a recommendation: enable prefix caching on /clinical-note-gen for identical prompts or use KV cache for repeated context. we estimate about 15-25% token reduction for your workload shape.
[02:55] Daniel: what's KV cache — is it the same as the KV cache in the runtime? wondering about stateful storage and eviction.
[03:03] Laura: yes, it's the runtime KV cache; apologies if on the doc it was labeled K-V cache or K V cache sometimes. it's local to serving nodes with a configurable TTL and eviction policy; for Dedicated we can extend persistence options.
[03:22] Priya: security wise we need audit logs and KMS integration; how do those show up?
[03:30] Samir: audit logs are in the console — under Security -> Audit Logs — you can export or stream to your SIEM. KMS integration is supported for Private and Dedicated; we also support BYOK with customer HSMs. we'll send the SOC2 and architecture pack after this.
[03:46] Maya: great. can you show cost attribution by model variant? we sometimes fall back to cheaper variants for lower latency steps.
[03:55] Laura: sure — filter by model variant. here's an example: you can see two variants side-by-side, cpu vs quantized GPU, with per-token cost estimate, avg latency. also there's a toggle to show billable token equivalence vs raw tokens.
[04:15] Daniel: does the console account for batching savings? our traffic has spikes, batching could amortize costs but increase latency.
[04:24] Laura: yes — Optimize includes batching estimates. in the per-route view there's an "impact simulator" where you can change batch size, quantization, or model and it projects cost and latency. for example, moving to 8-token batching reduces per-token cost by ~12% but p95 latency increases by ~40ms in this simulation.
[04:48] Priya: can we export the per-route CSV for finance?
[04:52] Laura: yep, export button top-right. you get tokens, costs, owner tags, and you can map routes to internal GL codes.
[05:02] Maya: on multitenancy — we route across regions; need per-region cost breakdown and ability to pin routes to specific regions for data residency.
[05:12] Samir: regions are first-class; per-route config can pin region or set routing policy. Console shows cost by region and you can set SLO routing policies so requests from eu customers hit EU instances only.
[05:29] Daniel: curious about quotas and cold start latency — do you show tail latency and cold starts?
[05:36] Laura: yes - we surface tail latencies and a cold-start metric. for Dedicated, cold-starts are minimized, and we have warmed pools. you'll see a separate chart for warm vs cold response times.
[05:50] Maya: talk me through the cost breakdown line items — infra, accelerator, redwood service fee, caching savings — what's included?
[05:59] Laura: the breakdown typically shows: raw accelerator compute estimate, infra overhead (network/storage), estimated caching savings, and Redwood service fee. when you commit to Dedicated we can replace the accelerator line with your committed rate. all estimations are clearly flagged as estimates and we show the assumptions used.
[06:21] Samir: i'll click into the cost model here — this is a sample cost spreadsheet embedded — note the assumptions: tokens per call distributions, seq length percentiles, and kernel/quantization profile used. small transcription note: sometimes the embedded spreadsheet titles come through oddly in exports.
[06:40] Daniel: regarding model selection, are you recommending specific quantization profiles? we have some fidelity requirements for clinical text.
[06:48] Laura: yes — Optimize suggests quantization profiles and models per-route. it shows expected regression probability and quality delta based on our eval sets. for clinical text we recommend 4-bit quantization with fallback to float16 in critical routes; we can set automatic fallback policies.
[07:10] Maya: any examples of actual customer savings?
[07:14] Samir: we have a case where a customer reduced token spend 28% via prefix caching + batching + switching to a quantized model for non-critical routes. happy to share an anonymized sheet.
[07:26] Priya: on the pilot — what's the best way to run a representative bench? we need realistic latency & throughput numbers.
[07:34] Samir: typical pilot: you provide sample traffic or a small replay; we run a 48–72 hour benchmark on Dedicated or Hosted with your profile, gather metrics, then run Optimize recommendations and show delta. Laura will coordinate.
[07:50] Laura: i'll follow up with a bench plan. also note we can run synthetic traffic with similar seq length distribution if needed.
[08:00] Daniel: can we restrict logs for PHI? we need to avoid retention of sensitive content.
[08:07] Laura: yes — you can configure retention policies, redaction hooks, and for Private deployments we support on-prem where logs never leave your VPC. for hosted we support token-level redaction and customer-managed keys for encryption at rest.
[08:24] Maya: what about SSO and RBAC — mapping routes to teams for cost ownership?
[08:30] Samir: SSO via SAML/OIDC, RBAC with fine-grained permissions, and you can tag routes with team owners. billing exports can then be mapped to cost centers automatically.
[08:46] Priya: competition question — how do you compare to Anthropic/OpAI on price and latency?
[08:53] Samir: depends on model; Redwood is an inference platform so if you self-host an open model you often get better unit economics. our runtime optimizations also improve latency vs naive hosting. for managed models the price comparison is model & infra dependent — we can run a side-by-side.
[09:12] Daniel: Anything else we need for procurement? standard security pack and compliance list?
[09:18] Samir: yes we'll send the SOC2, ISO certs, pen test summary, and the KMS + network diagrams.
[09:26] Maya: ok, let's talk concrete next steps — pilot timeline and pricing.
[09:30] Samir: agreed. action items: Laura sends security pack; Samir sends pricing; Daniel provides sample traffic. we aim to start benchmark week of 11/24.
[09:44] Priya: one more — can we get an estimate of engineering effort to integrate your routing policies into our platform?
[09:51] Laura: integration is typically a couple of days for API wiring + route tagging; if you want an agent we can scope that. we'll include a rough SOW in the follow-up.
[10:06] Maya: thanks all. that was helpful.
[10:10] Samir: thanks everyone, we'll follow up.

End of transcript.

References/shared artifacts: "Pricing worksheet (link)"; "SOC2 + architecture pack (link)"; "Pilot bench plan doc (link)"

Recap (auto): 1) Showed Console usage and per-route dashboards with cost breakdowns, batching/caching/quantization recommendations from Optimize. 2) Security questions: SOC2, KMS, VPC, audit logs addressed; Redwood to send security docs. 3) Pilot plan: NovaHealth to provide sample traffic; Redwood to run 48–72h benchmark; target week of 11/24. 4) Next steps assigned and pricing & SOW to follow.
